messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: ldply rbinds
parts:
Hi-

for some reason, the rbinding of returned objects to ldply is not intuitive to me and I wish it were a cbind. Any suggestions on how to get what I want other than transposes? Is there a reason not to allow the option in the call to ldply?

Thanks and best regards as always,

James

--

messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: Re: ldply rbinds
parts:
to my horror after spending too much time on this, i found that

data.frame(llply( ))

achieves my desired result of gathering all the data frames returned into a list into a single data frame via a cbind. I think I'd even done this before, still, it's not as intuitive as a cbind option to ldply seems.

James

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: ldply rbinds
parts:
Hi:

It also helps if the list components are named - if not, the resulting
data frame names are pretty ugly :) The 'solution' does make sense,
though, since a data frame is a special case of a list object.

I agree that ldply(listname, cbind) should behave as
data.frame(llply(listname)) does, though.

For the archives, here's a small example to see the problem in case
it's not obvious:

L <- vector('list', 3)
for(i in seq_along(L)) L[[i]] <- rnorm(5)

# These return matrices:
do.call(rbind, L)
do.call(cbind, L)

# Try to replicate the do.call() output in plyr:
laply(L, rbind)
laply(L, cbind)
t(laply(L, rbind))

names(L) <- c('V1', 'V2', 'V3')
ldply(L, rbind)
ldply(L, cbind)
data.frame(llply(L))

data.frame(do.call(rbind, L))
data.frame(do.call(cbind, L))

Dennis

your example is excellent. i had not observed the problem for laply. thank you for all your dedication! :)

trying several other approaches I was unable to get the original column names out, so the "solution" is the best thing I know of. I'm a huge advocate of using names in R. They are so good.

James
